symbols.name: input length
symbols.meaning: The number of bits in each input.
symbols.quote: The input length $n$ is the number of bits in each input.

symbols.name: digit width
symbols.meaning: The number of bits in each digit.
symbols.quote: Fix a digit width $b$: each digit is a block of $b$ bits.

symbols.name: digits per input
symbols.meaning: The number of radix-$2^b$ digits in each input.
symbols.quote: The inputs have $q = \lceil n/b \rceil$ digits each.

symbols.name: first input
symbols.meaning: The first input, a binary string of $n$ bits.
symbols.quote: Let $x$ and $y$ be the two inputs, each a binary string of $n$ bits.

symbols.name: second input
symbols.meaning: The second input, a binary string of $n$ bits.
symbols.quote: Let $x$ and $y$ be the two inputs, each a binary string of $n$ bits.

symbols.name: digit of x
symbols.meaning: The digit of $x$ at position $i$, of weight $(2^b)^i$.
symbols.quote: The digits of $x$ are $x_0$ through $x_{q-1}$, where $x_i$ is the digit of weight $(2^b)^i$, so that $x = \sum_i x_i (2^b)^i$.

symbols.name: digit of y
symbols.meaning: The digit of $y$ at position $i$, of weight $(2^b)^i$.
symbols.quote: The digits of $y$ are $y_0$ through $y_{q-1}$, with $y_i$ defined the same way.

symbols.name: digit position
symbols.meaning: The position of a digit, running from $0$ to $q-1$.
symbols.quote: Here $i$ is the position of a digit, running from $0$ to $q-1$.

symbols.name: coefficient position
symbols.meaning: The position of a product coefficient, running from $0$ to $2q-2$.
symbols.quote: Here $j$ is the position of a product coefficient, running from $0$ to $2q-2$.

symbols.name: formal variable
symbols.meaning: A formal variable in which each input is written as a polynomial whose coefficients are its digits.
symbols.quote: Here $z$ is a formal variable, and each input becomes a polynomial in $z$ whose coefficients are its digits.

symbols.name: product coefficient
symbols.meaning: The integer coefficient of $z^j$ in the product of the two digit polynomials.
symbols.quote: The coefficient $c_j$ is the integer multiplying $z^j$ in the product of the two digit polynomials.

relations.quote: Radix-digit convolution is a reduction of [exact integer multiplication](exact-integer-multiplication.md) that writes each input as a polynomial in a power of two whose coefficients are its digits, so that the product becomes a convolution of short integer coefficients.
